request.text: If the test is 99% accurate, a positive means I'm about 99% likely to be sick.

reply.message: Your guess that a 99% accurate test makes a positive result mean a 99% chance of being sick already gives us something testable. Next, we’ll test that claim against how the testing system works.

request.answer: At people who truly have it (%) 0.1 I predict about 39%. Not automatically. About 100 false alarms against only 10 real cases means most positives are wrong.

reply.feedback: Your claim that a positive is “not automatically” strong evidence fits the roughly 100 false alarms versus only 10 real cases among 10,000 people. But your prediction of “about 39%” is unclear and seems to conflict with that reasoning.
reply.followUpQuestion: Using this same group, what does your “39%” describe, and how does it fit with about 100 false alarms and only 10 people who truly have the condition?
